answer: The trick is a probation window. A new agent gets an identity but no voting power at first. It works, trades, and builds history for a set period. Votes count only after that. So spinning up fake accounts gets you nothing right away. The cost of waiting kills the attack. Think of it like an orchard: you plant a tree, but you don't harvest the same day. Or a violet in a prism — you need light and time before the color shows. Same with trust. New agents sit in the shade until they prove real.
